belief: My worth depends on staying wealthy.
origins: When a family, a profession, or a social circle measures people by what they own, we can learn that value equals net worth. A parent’s approval may have followed achievement, or a past loss may have made money feel like the only protection against shame. Over time the account balance can become a report card on the person.
teaches: Jesus said, “Watch out! Guard yourselves against every form of greed, for one’s life does not consist in the abundance of his possessions.” Scripture says we are fearfully and wonderfully made, and Paul tells the rich not to be conceited or to put their hope in the uncertainty of wealth, but in God, who richly provides all things for us to enjoy. Worth is a gift from our Creator, not a number we maintain. It cannot be raised by gain or lowered by loss.
self_statements: If I lost my money, I would be nothing.
I am only as valuable as my portfolio.
People respect me because of what I have.
I cannot stop earning or I will fall apart.
Without wealth I would have no identity.
Rest is for people who have not made it.
errors: Feeling secure when the numbers are high and worthless when they drop.
Seeing myself as either successful or a failure.
Calling myself a “winner” or “loser” based on money.
Assuming that losing wealth would mean losing everyone’s respect.
questions: What did I learn about worth growing up, and from whom?
If my finances changed tomorrow, what about me would remain?
What does God say my worth is based on?
Who loves me whether or not I have money?
What do I do to keep my balance high that is costing me peace?
What would it look like to receive my value as a gift?
truth: My worth was settled by God when He made me and by Christ when He died for me. It does not rise with my income or fall with my losses. I can steward wealth well and enjoy it, but I do not need it to prove that I matter.
hw_truths: I am valuable because God made me.
My worth does not go up or down with my balance.
I can enjoy wealth without needing it.
My hope is in God, not in money.
I can rest without losing my value.
Christ’s love is the one thing that cannot be lost.
log: Each day, write one thing that has value in you that has nothing to do with money, and note your peace from 0 to 10.
actions: List five things that are true of you that money cannot buy or take away.
Spend a half day away from checking accounts or earnings and notice how it feels.
Share where you have been tying your worth to money and ask for their view.
Say Luke 12:15 or Psalm 139:14 each morning for a week.
prayer: Lord, You made me and You know me. Free me from measuring myself by what I own. Help me hold wealth with open hands and rest in the worth You have already given me. Amen.
hw_questions: Where did I learn that wealth equals worth?
What would remain if my money were gone?
What does God say about my value?
Who loves me apart from my money?
What am I doing to protect my balance that costs me peace?
What is one way to rest in my worth today?
name_example: Sarah can write: “My life is more than my possessions, and I am valued by God.”
